380361.title: The quarter-distance isomorphism conjecture for Moufang 2-loops
380361.statement:

$$

M_K\leq M_L.

380727.title: Infinitely many odd-superbridge knots conjecture
380727.statement:
A knot $K$ has **superbridge index** $s[K]$, the minimum, over all knots $K'$ isotopic to $K$, of the maximum bridge number over unit directions. A knot with superbridge index $m$ is called an $m$-superbridge knot.

Nontrivial knots have superbridge index at least $3$, and the paper establishes that only finitely many $3$-superbridge knots exist, while infinitely many even-superbridge knots are known. This conjecture concerns the existence of infinitely many knots at every higher odd superbridge index.

$$
t(K_1\#K_2)=t(K_1)+t(K_2),
$$

then $E(K)$ has a minimal-genus Heegaard splitting that is weakly reducible. This proposes weak reducibility as a structural consequence of additive tunnel number, extending the examples and results discussed in the source; the conjecture is presented as open.

380919.title: Fiendish knot conjecture on tunnel-number additivity
380919.statement:
Let $K_1,K_2\subset S^3$, write $K=K_1\#K_2$, and let $E(K_i)$ denote the exterior of $K_i$. Let $t(K_i)$ denote the tunnel number, and call a Heegaard splitting **minimal genus** if its Heegaard surface has the smallest possible genus. A minimal-genus splitting has a **primitive meridian** when it admits the corresponding primitive-meridian configuration. **Fiendish knot conjecture.**

$$
t(K)=t(K_1)+t(K_2)+1
$$

if and only if both $E(K_1)$ and $E(K_2)$ do not have minimal-genus Heegaard splittings with primitive meridians. This conjecture characterizes the stated one-unit failure of tunnel-number additivity in terms of the absence of primitive meridians; the source attributes it to the case of fiendish knots and leaves it unresolved.

381166.title: The exponent-pair conjecture for weak Carmichael numbers

$$
{\mathcal P}_w(e',f')={\mathcal P}_w(e,f),

381451.statement:

382311.title: Castelnuovo bound conjecture for Gopakumar–Vafa invariants
382311.statement:
Let $X$ be a projective Calabi–Yau 3-fold of Picard number one and degree $n$. For integers $g$ and $d$, let $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}$ denote the genus $g$, degree $d$ Gopakumar–Vafa invariant of $X$.

**Castelnuovo bound conjecture.** The invariant vanishes when

$$
g > \frac{1}{2n}d^2+\frac{1}{2}d+1.
$$

This conjecture is the A-model conjecture used in the physical derivation of Gromov–Witten invariants of projective Calabi–Yau 3-folds. It predicts an effective vanishing range for the Gopakumar–Vafa invariants, supplying many of the initial conditions needed to determine higher-genus Gromov–Witten generating series; the source does not specify whether the conjecture has been resolved.
